title: At 39, Djokovic Wins First Match Since Wimbledon Despite Shoulder Treatment
summary:
Novak Djokovic is back in the win column. The 39-year-old Serbian beat Portugal's Nuno Borges 6-3, 7-6 (7-2) at the China Open in Beijing, collecting his first victory since he reached the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.

The result stretched Djokovic's unbeaten record at the tournament to 30 consecutive wins. He has won the China Open six times between 2009 and 2015 and is bidding to win it a record-extending seventh time. This was his first appearance at the event in 11 years, since 2015.

It was not a smooth win. Djokovic struggled in the second set, using his racket to help stretch his back between games and taking a medical timeout to receive treatment on his right shoulder. In August, he revealed that he has been dealing with an underlying health condition that causes particular problems in hot, humid conditions for "the past couple of years." He was far from his best against Borges, but he still battled through in one hour and 50 minutes.

Next, Djokovic will face Bu Yunchaokete of China in the second round. Bu is a wildcard, a player who received a special invitation to enter the tournament.

In other results, Great Britain's Katie Boulter advanced in the women's draw with a straight-set win over Japan's Mai Hontama. Boulter, 30, won 6-3, 6-4 and will now face Czech seventh seed Karolina Muchova in the next round.
why_it_matters: The story shows how athletes can win even when they are not at their best. It also shows how a long record, like Djokovic's streak at one tournament, can be part of a bigger sports story.
